events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Naguabo...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 552 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- At 550 PM AST, emergency management reported that road PR-31 km
8.0 remains closed due flooding waters.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A strong system is expected to move through the area Sunday night
into Monday. Temperatures below freezing combined with snow levels
below 1,000 ft are indicative of snowfall for upper elevations.
Mid-level southeasterly flow suggests potential for White Pass to be
sheltered from much of the precipitation, but would allow for ample
moisture to make it into the Haines Borough, falling as snow at the
border. The winter storm watch will be upgraded to a winter storm
warning for the upper elevations of the Haines Highway near Haines
Customs, and replaced with a winter weather advisory for the Klondike
Highway near White Pass.

* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 8 to 12
inches possible.

* WHERE...The Haines Highway, near Haines Border Crossing.

* WHEN...From 3 AM to 6 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The upper elevations of the Haines Highway,
near Haines Customs. Snow levels will steadily increase from around
500 ft to 2000 ft by Monday evening.

events.region: Coastal waters from Florence to Cape Blanco OR out 10 nm; Waters from Florence to Cape Blanco OR from 10 to 60 nm
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Very steep and hazardous seas 18 to 23 ft at 16 seconds
through tonight. Monday, south winds becoming 20 to 30 kt with
gusts up to 40 kt and steep wind-driven seas 10 to 14 ft.
Conditions gradually diminishing through Tuesday.

* WHERE...All areas north of Cape Blanco.

* WHEN...The Hazardous Seas Warning is in effect until 1 AM PST
Monday, followed by a Small Craft Advisory from 1 AM to 10 AM
PST Monday. A Gale Warning is then in effect from 10 AM to 10
PM PST Monday, followed by a Small Craft Advisory from 10 PM
Monday to 4 AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are expected. Bar
crossing will become exceptionally hazardous.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy mixed precipitation possible. Total snow accumulations
between 3 and 12 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze
to a tenth of an inch possible.

* WHERE...Ernestine.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A band of light snow is expected Monday
morning before tapering off Monday afternoon. A second round of
heavier snow, along with pockets of freezing rain mixed in, is
likely Monday evening through Tuesday morning. The highest snow and
ice totals are expected towards the north side of Thompson Pass
with the lower snow and ice totals expected towards Tonsina.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: East Turnagain Arm; Portage; Southern Kenai Mtns; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass; West Prince William Sound & Whittier
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy mixed precipitation possible. Total snow accumulations
between 3 and 7 inches for Whittier, Eastern Turnagain Arm,
Girdwood, and from Moose Pass to north of Seward. Total snow
accumulations between 5 and 10 inches of snow from Turnagain Pass
to Tern Lake, including the Hope Cutoff. Ice accumulations around a
light glaze possible from Turnagain Pass to Tern Lake and up to one
tenth of an inch from the Hope Cutoff to Hope. Easterly winds 55 to
70 mph possible for Eastern Turnagain Arm Tuesday morning.

* WHERE...East Turnagain Arm, and Western Prince William Sound.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong and complex weather system is
expected to move over the Kenai Peninsula beginning Monday morning.
Light snow to become steady by late Monday afternoon with snow,
heavy at times, Monday night through early Tuesday morning. East
winds from Prince William Sound will move through Whittier and
across Eastern Turnagain Arm Monday morning quickly changing the
snow at lower elevations to rain. At higher elevations, the snow
may become a wintry mix of snow, sleet, and freezing rain before
changing to rain. Any rain may also lead to slush and ponding of
water on roads. The easterly winds through Whittier and Eastern
Turnagain Arm may peak around 60 and 70 mph before diminishing
Tuesday afternoon.
